receipts.title: Observational equivalence of omitted implicit helper and incorrect neighboring fill in frozen-model skill repair
receipts.strongest_reduction: generic partial identification / fault localization remains a sufficient explanation until released matched units establish same-observable, incompatible repair targets
receipts.reason: The primary paper already defines IRF and RRO as distinct root causes, uses paired execution trajectories for attribution, and reports high automatic root-cause matching. The audited primary/full-text material does not expose a downloadable released trace/label asset containing matched units with the same observable outcome/trace/differential evidence but incompatible correct repair targets. The existence claim needed by this near-miss is therefore unsupported, not falsified.
avoid: rephrasing IRF-versus-RRO confusion as a new identifiability paper without released matched units
claiming trajectory ambiguity alone when the source already performs paired trajectory attribution
launching new expensive agent rollouts only to manufacture support for the problem formulation
receipts.reopen_only_if: A released or provenance-audited dataset supplies at least one non-synthetic matched unit in which observable outcome, execution trace, and differential evidence are information-equivalent while the correct repairs are incompatible (for example add omitted helper versus correct neighboring fill), and a generic partial-identification/fault-localization baseline using the same information does not absorb the residual claim.

receipts.title: Retrieval-Mediated Technical Debt in Fixed-Weight Self-Evolving Agent Runtimes
receipts.strongest_reduction: skill technical debt with persistent skill-library defects affecting future retrieval, composition, execution, and maintenance
receipts.reason: Current primary work already treats skill technical debt as a long-lived skill-library maintenance object whose defects degrade later retrieval, composition, and execution. Splitting the realization mechanism into validity/obsolescence and retrieval exposure changes the accounting of when debt is behaviorally realized, but does not yet define an irreducible paper object beyond the same technical-debt lifecycle under identical information.
avoid: renaming skill technical debt as retrieval-mediated debt
adding retrieval exposure as a second axis without an ex-ante residual prediction
claiming stored-but-unretrieved or obsolete-and-over-retrieved artifacts as novelty by itself
receipts.reopen_only_if: New primary evidence supports an ex-ante same-information prediction about access-mediated debt that a SkillOps-style technical-debt/maintenance model with the same artifact validity, retrieval, composition, execution, and maintenance observations cannot express; a two-axis relabeling alone does not reopen the basin.
